kernel_of_truth: The gear-motion defense has a genuine mechanical-engineering kernel: cam systems with non-circular profiles DO produce non-uniform angular velocity, and Fourier-decomposing a non-uniform circuit DOES generate sidebands at periods other than the fundamental. This is real mechanical physics, not a strawman. A dome defender who reaches for it is bringing a coherent kinematic idea — modulate angular velocity, get extra frequency components. The new paragraph acknowledges this kernel ('Mechanically that is true; engineering routinely builds cam systems with non-circular profiles, and Fourier-decomposing a non-uniform angular trajectory does yield higher harmonics') before showing why it fails on four independent grounds.
why_kernel_does_not_save_claim: Four independent failure modes, each fatal alone: (1) No gear equation is published in the dome codebase — the defense is 'something could do it', not 'the dome model does it'; (2) Parameter laundering: fitting N2/M2 = 0.1915 to any cam profile forces an asymmetry parameter ε_cam ≈ 0.0547, algebraically identical to Keplerian e ≈ 0.0549 — renaming the parameter does not reduce its arity; (3) Companion-harmonic constraint: the same eccentricity that gives N2/M2 ≈ 0.19 also yields L2/M2 ≈ 0.028 and 2N2/M2 ≈ 0.024 from a SINGLE parameter, and observations match all three — a gear-fit to N2 alone is a one-point fit requiring extra cam degrees of freedom to also fit L2 and 2N2; (4) Kinematic mismatch: non-uniform angular velocity at FIXED radius modulates timing not amplitude, but N2 is an amplitude sideband — generating it requires altitude variation, which would itself need a new free parameter (variation amplitude), undoing the savings.

patches.replace:
Doodson (1921).

A dome defender might counter that a gear-driven local moon need not move with uniform angular velocity — an eccentric cam, lobed track, or asymmetric drive train could in principle produce a non-uniform circuit and generate sidebands at periods other than the fundamental. Mechanically that is true; engineering routinely builds cam systems with non-circular profiles, and Fourier-decomposing a non-uniform angular trajectory does yield higher harmonics. But this defense imports the eccentricity problem rather than removing it. First, the dome publishes no gear equation: monitor.py, formulas.json, predictions.json, and inject_ai_layer.py contain no parameter for cam eccentricity, lobed-profile shape, or any other free quantity that could independently produce the ratio 0.19. Second, fitting N2/M2 = 0.1915 forces any cam profile to carry an asymmetry parameter εcam such that (7/2)·εcam ≈ 0.1915, which back-solves to εcam ≈ 0.0547 — algebraically identical to the Keplerian eccentricity it was meant to replace. Renaming the parameter does not reduce its arity; it is the same number under a different label. Third, the companion-harmonic constraint kills the one-point fit. The same Doodson 1921 expansion that gives N2/M2 ≈ 0.191 also yields L2/M2 ≈ 0.028 and 2N2/M2 ≈ 0.024 (Doodson 1921, Table II; cross-checked against the NOAA CO-OPS 37-constituent list), all three ratios derived from the SAME orbital eccentricity with no additional free parameter, and observations match these predicted ratios in the harmonic analysis of every long-record tide gauge. A gear-driven defense must reproduce the full Doodson family — not just N2 — from a single cam profile. Doing so without an eccentricity-equivalent parameter would require multiple additional cam degrees of freedom, multiplying rather than reducing the model's structural debt. Fourth, the substitution fails kinematically. Non-uniform angular velocity at fixed radius modulates the timing of M2 forcing peaks but not their amplitude; the N2 constituent, distinguished from M2 in modern harmonic analyses by its independent amplitude evolution at the 27.55-day anomalistic period, encodes an amplitude variation. Producing amplitude variation requires the moon's distance from Earth to oscillate — the very feature that motivates the Keplerian eccentricity in standard theory. The dome's published altitude for the local moon is the fixed value 2,534 km, with no altitude-variation parameter specified anywhere in the codebase. A gear-driven defense that keeps the moon at constant altitude cannot generate a true amplitude sideband; one that allows altitude variation must specify the variation amplitude, restoring the same single free parameter under a different name.

anticipated_objections.objection: The L2/M2 ≈ 0.028 and 2N2/M2 ≈ 0.024 numbers depend on the orbital eccentricity AND on additional orbital geometry (lunar inclination, solar perturbations). It's not strictly true that they come from 'a single parameter'.
anticipated_objections.response: Conceded that the full Doodson expansion has multiple parameters (e, inclination, solar forcing). The paragraph's claim is the weaker and correct one: among the eccentricity-dependent constituents, N2, L2, and 2N2 all come from the SAME orbital eccentricity. Fitting one cam asymmetry to N2 leaves L2 and 2N2 unfit unless additional cam parameters are introduced. The argument is about the SHARED eccentricity dependence, not about all parameters being identical.

anticipated_objections.objection: Point 4 (FM vs AM distinction) is not airtight: a sufficiently complex cam can produce both timing and amplitude modulation of the projected tidal forcing on a flat-Earth observer.
anticipated_objections.response: The paragraph already acknowledges this implicitly by routing through 'fixed radius'. A cam that varies effective radius (lobed cam) does produce amplitude modulation — but then it imports altitude variation, which is point 4's other half: the dome's published altitude is fixed at 2,534 km. A radius-varying cam would require a NEW free parameter (variation amplitude), restoring the parameter-laundering problem. The argument is internally consistent.

anticipated_objections.objection: What if the dome defender simply says 'we will specify the cam profile in a future version'?
anticipated_objections.response: Standard escape-hatch response: an unspecified future model is not a current prediction. The same rebuttal applies as in Part 3.1b's trivial-transcription test — a claim of confirmation requires a current derivation. WIN-051 is currently listed as a confirmed prediction; the gear-motion defense, if invoked, demotes it to a deferred conjecture pending a published cam equation.
